## A dataset for today's workshop

- 24 items of the Authentic Happiness Inventory (AHI)
- 20 items of the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression (CES-D) scale
- measured on 1 to 6 measurement occasions

```{webr-r}
?ds4psy::posPsy_AHI_CESD

pospsy <- ds4psy::posPsy_AHI_CESD
```

## DRY: Don't repeat yourself

## Repeated application of the same function

CES-D is usually measured on a scale of 0-3, in our dataset it has a scale of 1-4:

```{webr-r}
range(pospsy$cesd01)
```

To recode it, I could do something like that:

```{webr-r}
pospsy$cesd01r <- pospsy$cesd01 - 1 
pospsy$cesd02r <- pospsy$cesd02 - 1 
pospsy$cesd03r <- pospsy$cesd03 - 1 
pospsy$cesd04r <- pospsy$cesd04 - 1 
```

However, this is repetitive and error prone.

## Writing Functions

```{webr-r}

recode_cesd <- function(cesd_var) {
  cesd_var - 1
}
```

## Making code easier to read

Easier to read code = easier comprehension

There are two measures you can take to improve your code quality

- good names
- consistent code style

## Naming things

Naming things is hard - so hard that books are written about it:

![Book Naming Things](images/naming_things_book.PNG)

## How to pick good names?

- descriptive
- prioritize reader's understanding over shortness or machine compatibility
- follow a standard naming convention

## Naming conventions

Two most commonly used conventions:

:snake: snake_case

:camel: camelCase

## Examples for bad names

::: incremental
`x`
:::

## What might be bad about names like these ?

`c`, `df`, `data`

::: incremental
They are also names of base functions
:::

## Styling code with `lintr`

[lintr](https://lintr.r-lib.org/) conducts static code analysis on your R files.

``` r
#| eval: false
# Style one file
lintr::lint()

# A whole directory or R project
lintr::lint_dir()
```

## Styling code with `lintr`

```{webr-r}
names(lintr::linters_with_defaults())
```

## Beyond `lintr`

`lintr` gives recommendations but does not change code. These tools can style your code directly:

- [Air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/)
- [styler](https://styler.r-lib.org/)

::: callout-warning
Caution: these tools change your code without asking again
:::
